To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the voltage-gated K+-channels Kv12.1, Kv12.3 and Kv12.2 have been overlooked in the brain, due to the lack of specific pharmacological agents and the absence of genetically modified mice that express the respective channel proteins in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner.
we identified a unique mode shift in human Kv12. 1 channels that is distinct from Kv11.1 and that 4-AP activates Kv12.1, whereas NS1643 inhibits Kv12.1 currents.

the voltage-gated potassium channel subunit Kv12.1 has a unique biophysical and a pharmacological profile and that the broad-spectrum potassium antagonist 4-AP activates Kv12.1 currents, whereas it inhibits Kv11.1 currents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biophysical and pharmacologic characterization of the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv12.1.
the molecular mechanisms of the regulation of the activity of the neuronal Kv12 channels.
the identification of the biophysical and pharmacologic properties of the human Kv12.2 potassium channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Kv12.3 channels are the most likely candidate for the Kv12-mediated currents observed in hippocampal pyramidal neurons.
4-AP is a nonselective K+ channel activator and that NS1643 is a nonselectve K+ channel inhibitor.
Kv12.3 channels are expressed in the brain, and their function is unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified unique properties of Kv12 channels and established experimental protocols to characterize native currents.
we identified a new pharmacological profile for Kv12.1.
Kv12. 1 channels can be distinguished from Kv11.1 channels through mode shift and differential pharmacology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Kv12 channels may be overlooked in native cell types, and that their identification can benefit from the unique biophysical and electrophysiological properties of Kv12 channels.
mode shift of Kv12.2 and Kv12.1 can be used as a signature property to discriminate these channels from other Kv channels in native cells.
mode shift of activation can be used to distinguish between Kv12.1- and Kv11.2-mediated currents.
